# BurpFree ↔ Burp Suite workflow compatibility

This matrix maps the practitioner-visible workflows people reach for
when they open an intercepting-proxy suite onto their BurpFree
equivalents. Statuses: ✅ implemented · 🟡 partial · 🔲 planned.

## Core traffic engine

| Workflow                              | BurpFree equivalent                                                   | Status | Tested |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----: | :----: |
| HTTP/1.1 proxy                        | `burpfree-proxy::server`                                              | ✅ | ✅ |
| HTTPS MITM + dynamic certs            | `burpfree-ca`, `burpfree-proxy::server`                               | ✅ | ✅ |
| HTTP/2 proxy                          | — (seams in place for `h2` crate)                                     | 🔲 | — |
| HTTP/3 proxy                          | —                                                                     | 🔲 | — |
| CONNECT tunneling                     | `burpfree-proxy::server`                                              | ✅ | ✅ |
| Self-loop guard (refuse own listener) | `burpfree-proxy::server::is_self_target`                              | ✅ | ✅ |
| Multiple listeners                    | `burpfree-proxy::server`                                              | ✅ | 🟡 |
| Upstream direct                       | `burpfree-proxy::upstream`                                            | ✅ | ✅ |
| Upstream HTTP CONNECT                 | `burpfree-proxy::upstream`                                            | ✅ | ✅ |
| Upstream SOCKS5                       | `burpfree-proxy::upstream`                                            | ✅ | ✅ |
| Interception (hold / forward / drop)  | `burpfree-proxy::interceptor`                                         | ✅ | ✅ |
| Intercept pane uses rich MessageEditor | Shared `web/src/MessageEditor` component — pretty / raw / hex view, Ctrl+F search, right-click Decoder transforms, Inspector sidebar, Ctrl+Enter forwards | ✅ | ✅ |
| WebSocket frame interception          | `burpfree-proxy::ws_interceptor` queue + `ws_replay` hook + WebSocket > Interceptor sub-tab | ✅ | ✅ |
| WebSocket history pane (sessions + messages) | ProxyPanel WebSockets sub-tab reads `ws_sessions_list` + `ws_messages_list`, 2-pane view with auto-refresh, direction / opcode / timestamp / preview columns, truncation marker | ✅ | ✅ |
| WebSocket intercept Drop-all + per-frame context menu | `WsInterceptor::drop_all()` mirrors `release_all` — drains the pending VecDeque while resolving each responder with `Verdict::Drop`, returns count. Tauri cmd `ws_intercept_drop_all`. WebSocketPanel `WsInterceptorPane` grows a `Drop all (N)` danger button next to Forward-all (confirm first), and each queued frame row carries a right-click `FloatingMenu` with Release / Drop / Copy preview text / Send to Comparer left+right (fires `burpfree:comparer-load` with a `ws outbound text #N` label). Test `drop_all_resolves_every_pending_to_drop` queues 3 frames and asserts all three futures resolve to `Verdict::Drop`; proxy suite 41 passed (+1) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Interception rule engine (match-type + and/or operator) | `burpfree-proxy::interceptor::{InterceptRule, InterceptRules}` | ✅ | ✅ |
| Intercept rules: per-rule live hit counter | Mirror of R60's match/replace hit counter, now on the interception side. Pairs with R55's preview (preview shows what WOULD fire; this shows what IS firing against live traffic). Backend: `Interceptor` grew a top-level `hits: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<String, u64>>>` field alongside the existing `state: Arc<Mutex<State>>` Arc. Deliberately NOT on `InterceptRules` because `set_request_rules` / `set_response_rules` replace the inner `rules_request` / `rules_response` wholesale on every save — storing the counter inside would zero it on each Save click. The derived `Clone` keeps the Arc shared so `h.interceptor.clone()` sites all over the Tauri layer see the same counter. Refactored `InterceptRules::evaluate_request` / `evaluate_response` to delegate to new `pub(crate) evaluate_request_counted(req, in_scope) -> (Option<bool>, Vec<String>)` + `evaluate_response_counted(req, resp, in_scope) -> (Option<bool>, Vec<String>)` which do a single pass collecting the aggregate decision AND the ordered IDs of enabled rules whose `effect` (post-relationship) was true. One pass means hit counts stay in lockstep with what the proxy actually inspected (no risk of a second walk diverging). `maybe_intercept_request_with_scope` + `maybe_intercept_response_with_request` call the counted variant, bump hits via `self.bump_hits(&hit_ids)` BEFORE checking the final decision — so a rule that fires inside a losing AND chain still counts its own firing; the hit tracks per-rule contribution, not the aggregate hold/forward outcome. Public API on `Interceptor`: `rule_hit_snapshot() -> HashMap<String, u64>` clones the current map (missing keys = never fired, UI renders 0); `clear_rule_hits()` wipes it; private `bump_hits(ids)` early-returns on empty slice so the hot path skips the lock, otherwise walks ids and `.saturating_add(1)`s each entry so overflow becomes a visible plateau rather than silent wrap. Tauri cmds `interceptor_rules_hits() -> HashMap<String, u64>` + `interceptor_rules_hits_clear() -> ()` registered after `interceptor_rules_preview` in `main.rs`; both use the `let snap = h.interceptor.rule_hit_snapshot(); Ok(snap)` E0597-dodge pattern because the direct `Ok(h.interceptor.rule_hit_snapshot())` would drop `h` before the `RwLockReadGuard` temporary — same footgun as R57/R58/R60. Frontend: `interceptorRulesHits()` + `interceptorRulesHitsClear()` bindings in `api.ts`. `InterceptRulesEditor` grew `hits: Record<string, number>` + `hitsBusy: boolean` state, 2s polling useEffect (silent on no-project / cmd-race errors — keeps the stale snapshot so a transient blip doesn't blank the column), `resetHits()` handler. Rules table grew a right-aligned `Hits` column with its own 60px colgroup entry between Condition and the action buttons; zero rows render in dim-faint grey, non-zero rows render in accent colour with bold weight; hover tooltip switches between "No fires yet. Each proxy request/response that passes while intercept is ON evaluates this rule; the counter bumps whenever its `effect` is true (independent of the aggregate decision)." and "This rule has fired N time(s) since the last Reset." Toolbar grew a `Reset hits (N)` button annotated with the live total so the operator sees how much state the click will wipe — disabled when total is 0 so a stale click can't flash the counter at 0. Empty-row colSpan bumped 6 → 7 to span the new column. Shared one `hits` map across both directions because rule IDs are globally unique, so switching the direction toggle doesn't force a re-poll. Test `intercept_rule_hits_increment_on_fire`: 2-rule AND chain (Host matches `example.com`, Method matches POST), fires GET on example.com → rule 1 effect true + rule 2 effect false → aggregate `Some(false)` so no parking, but r1's hit=1 and r2 absent (proves fire-in-losing-chain still counts); fires POST on example.com → both effects true → aggregate `Some(true)` → parks the message (resolved via Forward spawn), r1=2 r2=1; `clear_rule_hits()` empties the map; proxy crate 46 (+1 from R60's 45), workspace suite 425 (+1 from R60's 424) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Intercept rules: Preview on sample | Backend: new `PreviewReport { decision: Option<bool>, rules: Vec<RulePreview> }` + `RulePreview { id, enabled, operator, match_type, relationship, condition, matched, effect }` structs (Serialize) on `crates/burpfree-proxy/src/interceptor.rs`. Refactored `eval_rule_request` / `eval_rule_response` to delegate to new `pub(crate) rule_matched_request` / `rule_matched_response` helpers so Preview and the live intercept pipeline can't drift silently; both callers now share one truth for the per-match-type predicate. `InterceptRules::preview_request(&self, req, in_scope)` + `preview_response(&self, req, resp, in_scope)` walk every rule (disabled included — they show hypothetical effect so operators can see what they'd do if flipped on), compute matched (raw) + effect (post-relationship) per rule, aggregate decision using the same AND/OR fold as `evaluate_*` but skipping disabled rules so the badge matches live-run semantics. Tauri cmd `interceptor_rules_preview(args: { direction, url, method?, in_scope }) -> PreviewReport` builds the Request via `Request::new(method.unwrap_or("GET"), &url)` with the parse error surfaced inline; request direction calls `request_rules().preview_request(…)`, response direction pairs with an empty `Response::new(200)` so response-visible match types (HasBody, HeaderPresent) have something concrete to probe. Frontend: `PreviewReport` + `RulePreview` TS types in `api.ts` plus the `interceptorRulesPreview` binding. `InterceptRulesEditor` grows a Preview-on-sample section below the rules table: method dropdown, monospaced URL input, in-scope checkbox, Run button (label switches to "Run (saved rules only)" with a hint when the editor is dirty since the preview targets the persisted ruleset), aggregate decision badge (red HOLD / green FORWARD / dim "no rules enabled"), inline error line for bad URLs, per-rule result table with Enabled / Op / Match type / Relationship / Condition / Matched / Effect columns (disabled rows ghosted at 50% opacity; effect-true rows get a subtle accent background so the chain of HOLD contributions is visible at a glance). URL + method + in-scope state persist for the editor's lifetime so iterating rule → save → preview doesn't force the operator to re-type the sample every pass. Test `preview_report_tracks_matched_effect_and_decision`: three-rule chain (Host regex `^api\.`, Method != POST AND, InScope OR disabled) against GET `api.example.com/u` asserts matched + effect per rule and decision = Some(true); flip method to POST, decision becomes Some(false) via the AND fold dropping the chain; all-disabled chain returns decision = None so the UI badges "no rules enabled" instead of implying forward. Proxy crate 43 (+1 from R54's 42), workspace suite 416 (+1 from R54's 415) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Repeater: bounded per-tab history + Clear history button + context-menu entry | Both a memory-leak fix and an operator-ergonomics addition. Backend: `RepeaterTab::history: Vec<RepeaterSend>` was previously unbounded — any long probing session (think an operator stepping through 10 payload variants to narrow a bug) could grow the Vec arbitrarily and bloat the persisted `repeater.json` + runtime memory indefinitely. Added `pub const MAX_HISTORY_PER_TAB: usize = 500` + free `fn trim_history(h: &mut Vec<RepeaterSend>)` right before the `Repeater` struct in `crates/burpfree-engines/src/repeater.rs`. trim_history drops the OLDEST entries via `drain(0..n)` so the newest sends keep sitting at the tail where every UI call site reads them (`history[history.len() - 1]`, the HistoryStrip's forward-iteration render, etc. — nothing shifts around). Wired into BOTH push sites: `send()` AND `follow_redirect()`. 500 entries ≈ a few MB per tab even assuming 10 KB bodies — enough for a day's worth of probes, cheap enough the trim is invisible. Also added `pub fn clear_tab_history(&self, id: TrafficId) -> bool` that write-locks tabs, calls `h.history.clear()` in place, returns true iff the tab existed, and calls `save()` so the on-disk JSON matches memory. Everything else on the tab (template / name / pinned / colour / group / order / follow-redirects override) survives the clear — only the Sends Vec is nuked. Tauri cmd `repeater_tab_clear_history(id) -> bool` in `commands.rs` right before `repeater_remove`, registered in `main.rs` after `repeater_duplicate_tab`. Frontend: `repeaterTabClearHistory(id)` TS binding in `api.ts` after `repeaterDuplicateTab`. `HistoryStrip` grew an `onClearHistory: (id: number) => void` prop; a `Clear history` ghost-danger button renders at the end of the strip (right of the diff clear), always available (not gated by diff state) so the operator can wipe regardless of selection. Click confirms `Clear ${n} responses from "${tab.name}"? The tab itself stays.` before the backend call. Parent `clearTabHistory(id)` helper calls the Tauri cmd, silently returns on `existed=false` (stale id), refreshes tabs, and if the active tab was the one cleared also resets `sendIndex`, blanks `respRaw`, and clears `diffA / diffB / diffReport` so the response pane + diff controls match the empty-history state. Tab FloatingMenu grew a `Clear history (N)` danger entry right after `Copy last response (raw)` with the same confirm dialog + a "wipe sends, keep tab" hint, disabled when the tab's history is empty. Two tests: `trim_history_drops_oldest_over_cap` (pure, no network) builds Vec<RepeaterSend>s via struct literal — asserts under-cap no-op, at-cap no-op (first entry at index 0 preserved), MAX+20 drops oldest 20 (first retained send has the elapsed_ms it got at index 20) and preserves tail (`history[MAX-1]` is still the latest). `clear_tab_history_wipes_sends_but_keeps_tab` fires 2 real sends against a mock listener (echoing 200 OK), asserts history=2, calls clear_tab_history, asserts history=0 while name="probe" + template.host="127.0.0.1" + pinned=true + color="#ff8844" all survive; non-existent id returns false; drop + reload the Repeater from `r.json` and assert history=0 persists (save() path exercised). Engines crate 222 (+2 from R63's 220), workspace suite 429 (+2 from R63's 427) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Repeater cancel-all (panic button) + per-tab cancel from context menu + inflight resync | Backend: `Repeater::cancel_all() -> usize` iterates every entry in `self.inflight.read().values()`, fires `notify_waiters()` on each `Arc<Notify>`, returns the number of woken tabs. Panic button for `send_group_parallel` fan-outs that start starving the target. `Repeater::inflight_ids() -> Vec<TrafficId>` returns a snapshot of every mid-flight tab so the UI can resync Cancel-button state on panel re-mount (reload / navigation / tab switch) — the useState default is an empty Set which would otherwise leave Cancel disabled until the next locally-initiated send. Tauri cmds `repeater_cancel_all() -> usize` + `repeater_inflight_ids() -> Vec<i64>` registered alongside `repeater_cancel`. Frontend: new `repeaterCancelAll` + `repeaterInflightIds` bindings in `api.ts`. RepeaterPanel's initial mount effect does `const ids = await api.repeaterInflightIds(); if (ids.length > 0) setInflight(new Set(ids))` so Cancel buttons highlight correctly for sends started before this mount. New `cancelAll()` + `cancelTab(id)` helpers alongside `cancelActive()`; cancel-all re-uses the per-send finally-block cleanup path so the inflight Set reconciles naturally one entry at a time. Toolbar grows a danger `Cancel all (N)` button that only renders when `inflight.size > 1` (hidden for single-tab in-flight since the main Cancel button already handles that case). Ctrl+Shift+Backspace hits the same path via the existing cancel keydown handler (ctrl∨meta + Backspace with `e.shiftKey` branch). Tab FloatingMenu grows a danger `Cancel send` entry right after `Duplicate tab`, disabled when `!inflight.has(tabMenu.data.id)` with a `no send in flight` hint. Shortcuts help page + hint strip updated to list both `Ctrl+Backspace` and `Ctrl+Shift+Backspace`. Test `cancel_all_wakes_every_in_flight_send`: 3 concurrent `send()`s against a hung-listener (accepts bytes then holds the socket on `std::future::pending()`), waits 150ms for all Notifys to register, asserts `inflight_ids().len() == 3`, calls cancel_all (returns 3), awaits every send, asserts each result's error contains `"cancel"`, confirms the inflight map is empty after resolution, and a follow-up `cancel_all()` on the empty map returns 0 (no-op); engines crate 213 (+1 from R52's 212), workspace suite 414 (+1 from R52's 413) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Repeater cancel in-flight send | `Repeater` grew an `inflight: Arc<RwLock<HashMap<TrafficId, Arc<tokio::sync::Notify>>>>`; `send()` and `follow_redirect()` call a `register_inflight(id)` helper that installs a fresh `Notify`, then race the HTTP future against `notify.notified()` under `tokio::select!` — on cancel the client future is dropped mid-await (closes the socket), and the returned `RepeaterSend` carries `error = Some("send cancelled")` so the UI sees a normal history row instead of a Promise reject. `clear_inflight(id, own)` uses `Arc::ptr_eq` so an overlapping second send that overwrote the slot keeps its own cancel channel rather than being accidentally cleared by the finishing first send. `pub fn cancel(&self, id) -> bool` reads the map and fires `notify_waiters()` (vs `notify_one` so parallel sends on the same tab all unpark together); returns `true` iff an entry existed. Tauri cmd `repeater_cancel(id) -> bool` forwards to the engine; API binding `api.repeaterCancel(id)` plumbed. RepeaterPanel toolbar tracks `inflight: Set<number>` and flips the primary Send button into a red Cancel button while the active tab has a request on the wire — the handler calls `api.repeaterCancel(active)` and the finally-block of `send()` clears the id from the Set. Ctrl+Backspace fires the same cancel from anywhere in the Repeater panel (modifier set is `(ctrl ∨ meta) + Backspace`, scoped per-mount so it doesn't bleed into Comparer/Scanner). The hint text under the request editor updates to "Ctrl+Enter to send · Ctrl+Backspace to cancel", and shortcuts.ts gains a `scoped("repeater")` entry. Any Rust-level error whose message contains "cancel" is swallowed on the frontend to future-proof against the Promise-reject path (today it never fires). Test `cancel_aborts_in_flight_send` spawns a listener that drains the client bytes then holds the socket on `std::future::pending()`, launches cancel from a 100ms-delayed task, asserts `send.error.contains("cancel")`, `send.response.is_none()`, history length 1, and that a follow-up cancel returns false now the inflight slot is free; engines crate 209 (+1 from R48's 208), workspace 409 (+1 from 408) | ✅ | ✅ |
| TLS pass-through list for cert-pinned clients | `ServerConfig::tls_passthrough` is a shared `Arc<RwLock<Vec<String>>>` consulted by `handle_connect` right after the CONNECT line is parsed; matched hosts (case-insensitive substring via `is_passthrough_host`) skip the leaf-cert mint and `TlsAcceptor::accept` and instead open a raw `TcpStream` to the origin with `connect_timeout`-bounded dial, then pump bytes both ways via `tokio::io::copy` (client→origin and origin→client) under `tokio::try_join!` — no MITM so pinned mobile apps / IoT clients that would otherwise reject our root CA still get an end-to-end TLS tunnel while bytes flow through the proxy. `ProjectConfig::tls_passthrough: Vec<String>` persists the list in `config.json` (opt-in: empty by default, `#[serde(default)]` keeps old projects working). `AppState::tls_passthrough` mirrors the Arc so Tauri cmds `tls_passthrough_get` / `tls_passthrough_set(list)` can swap the pattern list live — the running proxy picks up new entries on the next CONNECT without a restart. ProxyPanel `OptionsPane` grows a dedicated "TLS pass-through" section below the TLS-interception checkbox: a monospaced `<textarea rows=6>` showing one host-pattern per line, a count badge, an unsaved-changes indicator, and a Save button that only lights up when the buffer differs from the last-persisted value; set-side trims each entry and drops empty lines so operator typos never silently match everything. Unit test `passthrough_host_substring_case_insensitive` confirms the predicate (patterns with trimmed whitespace, upper/lower casing, and partial matches); workspace suite 408 passed (+1 from R47's 407) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Intercept queue: Forward all / Drop all + per-row context menu | `Interceptor::resolve_all(action)` on the engine walks every pending entry via the single-item `resolve()` path so each waiting proxy connection sees a decision (contrast with `clear_all` which drops silently and starves receivers). `get_original(id)` surfaces the queued raw bytes without resolving so Send-to-Repeater / Send-to-Comparer / Copy-as-cURL work while the intercept is still held. Tauri cmds `interceptor_resolve_all(action)` + `interceptor_show(id)`. ProxyPanel intercept toolbar grew `Forward all (N)` + `Drop all (N)` buttons (Drop-all behind a confirm; both disabled when queue is empty). Each pending row has a FloatingMenu context menu with Forward / Drop / Send to Repeater (requests only — adds a new tab via `repeaterAddTab` + fires `burpfree:nav` → repeater) / Send to Comparer (left/right slots via `burpfree:comparer-load`) / Copy URL / Copy as cURL / Copy as PowerShell (`fromUrlAndRaw` + `buildCurl`/`buildPowerShell`). Tests `resolve_all_forwards_every_pending` (3 pending ⇒ 3 Forward decisions delivered) + `peek_raw_returns_bytes_without_resolving` (get_original is non-destructive; unknown ids yield None); proxy suite now 40 passed | ✅ | ✅ |
| Match/Replace (regex + case-insensitive) | `burpfree-proxy::matchreplace`                                     | ✅ | ✅ |
| Match/Replace per-rule live hit counter | Pairs with R56's preview (preview shows what WOULD fire; this shows what DID). Backend: `MatchReplaceEngine` grew `hits: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<String, u64>>>` with `#[serde(skip, default = "default_hits")]`. Auto-derived `Clone` preserves the Arc — crucial because `h.match_replace.read().clone()` is called all over the Tauri layer and fragmented counters would be useless. Both apply paths (`apply_request_with_response` + `apply_response_with_request`) now call `self.bump_hit(&rule.id)` immediately after `try_apply_*` returns `Some(true)`; `preview_*` deliberately does NOT touch the counter so dry-runs can't lie. New methods: `update_rules(rules)` swaps the rule set while leaving `self.hits` intact (used by the save path so operator config writes don't zero the trail); `hit_snapshot()` clones the current counter map (keys absent for never-fired rules so a fresh engine renders cleanly); `clear_hits()` zeroes everything; private `bump_hit` uses `.saturating_add(1)` so overflow becomes a visible plateau rather than silent wrap. Tauri cmd `match_replace_set` now serialises the rules Vec BEFORE moving it into `update_rules(engine.rules)` so persistence works + Arc sharing is preserved (the old `*h.match_replace.write() = engine.clone()` replaced the whole engine, nuking the counter). Two new cmds: `match_replace_hits() -> HashMap<String, u64>` (materialises the snapshot into a local before Ok(...) to dodge rustc's E0597 on `h` dropping while a `RwLockReadGuard` temporary is still alive — a lesson for every future `let h = state.require()?` + `Ok(h.something.read().method())` call site) and `match_replace_hits_clear() -> ()`. Frontend: `matchReplaceHits()` + `matchReplaceHitsClear()` bindings; `MatchReplacePane` grew `hits: Record<string, number>` state polled every 2s inside its own useEffect (silent on no-project / cmd-race errors so a stale snapshot is kept rather than clearing the column). Rules table grew a right-aligned `Hits` column between `R` and the action buttons: zero rows render in dim-faint grey, non-zero rows render in the accent colour with bold weight; hover tooltip changes between "No fires yet. Live traffic that passes this rule's gate (enabled + scope + host filter + predicate) and matches its pattern bumps this counter." and "This rule has fired N time(s) since the last Reset." Toolbar grew a `Reset hits (N)` button annotated with the total so the operator sees how much state the click will clear — disabled when no fires yet so a stale click can't flash the counter at 0. Test `hits_increment_on_apply_but_not_on_preview`: 2-rule engine (add-audit fires, never-fires misses), applies 3× then asserts `snap["add-audit"] == 3` + miss-rule absent, previews 2× and asserts counter unchanged, clones the engine and applies through the clone and asserts the counter now 4 (proves Arc sharing), `update_rules([])` preserves the count, `clear_hits()` empties the map; proxy crate 45 (+1 from R59's 44), workspace suite 424 (+1 from R59's 423) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Match/Replace per-rule last-fire timestamp | Follow-up to R60's hit counter — operators iterating on a rule chain want to see not just how often a rule fires but when the last fire landed, so a "ruleset went quiet after a config push" bug is spottable without reading tracing logs. Backend: `MatchReplaceEngine` grew `last_fire: Arc<parking_lot::Mutex<HashMap<String, i64>>>` alongside the existing `hits` Arc, same `#[serde(skip, default = "default_last_fire")]` pattern so the field is runtime-only and legacy project files round-trip through serde. `bump_hit()` now stamps `burpfree_core::traffic::now_ms()` into `last_fire` after incrementing the counter — single call site keeps the two maps in lockstep without an extra lock dance. New `last_fire_snapshot() -> HashMap<String, i64>` getter clones the map (same convention as `hit_snapshot`: absent keys = never fired, UI renders "—"). `clear_hits()` now wipes both maps atomically so Reset in the UI stays coherent — the operator never ends up with "0 fires but Last fire = 2m ago" after a reset. Tauri cmd `match_replace_last_fires() -> HashMap<String, i64>` added right after `match_replace_hits` with the same E0597-dodge pattern (`let snap = h.match_replace.read().last_fire_snapshot(); Ok(snap)`); registered in main.rs invoke_handler. Frontend: `matchReplaceLastFires()` binding in api.ts. `MatchReplacePane` grew `lastFires: Record<string, number>` state; the existing 2s hits poller was rewritten to `Promise.all([matchReplaceHits, matchReplaceLastFires])` so both snapshots arrive in the same tick (backend serves each from the same engine lock so lockstep is best-effort, but close enough for a "last fire" display); a separate 30s wall-clock `setTickTock` pulse re-renders the humanized labels so a "2m ago" cell on an idle rule advances to "3m ago" without needing a backend round-trip. `resetHits()` now clears both the hits and lastFires state after the cmd returns so the UI reflects the backend wipe immediately. Rules table grew a right-aligned `Last fire` column after Hits with a mono 11px cell; `humanizeAge(tsMs)` returns "—" for 0/undefined, "just now" under 1s, otherwise the biggest unit that fits ("5s ago" / "2m ago" / "1h ago" / "3d ago") — short strings because the column is narrow; the exact timestamp lives in the hover tooltip via `new Date(ms).toLocaleString()`. Faded colour when "—", normal text colour when stamped so the eye picks out dormant rules at a glance. Empty-state row colSpan bumped 8 → 9. Test `last_fire_timestamp_stamps_on_apply_only`: 2-rule engine (add-audit fires, never-fires misses), applies once and asserts the add-audit timestamp falls between before/after wall-clock capture, miss-rule stays absent; sleeps 5ms + runs `preview_request` twice and asserts timestamp unchanged (dry-run contract); sleeps 5ms + applies again, new timestamp >= old; `clear_hits` wipes both maps; clone of the engine applies through the clone and the original sees the stamp (Arc sharing). Proxy crate 46 (+1 from R68's 45 ignoring R62 revert noise), workspace suite 441 (+1 from R68's 440), bundle 569.08 KB (+0.99), binary 223 MB (+0.1) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Match/Replace Preview on sample | Mirror of R55's intercept preview, but for the match/replace engine. Backend: new `RuleHit { id, name, enabled, scope_matched, fired }` + `MatchReplacePreview { before_wire, after_wire, rules_applied, net_mutations }` structs. Refactored `apply_request_with_response` + `apply_response_with_request` to share two new helpers — `try_apply_request(engine, rule, req, resp?) -> Option<bool>` + `try_apply_response(engine, rule, resp, host, req?) -> Option<bool>` — that return `None` when a gate (enabled / scope / host_filter / predicate_script) drops the rule and `Some(fired)` when apply was attempted (the inner bool is whether the target actually mutated the message). Preview and the live pipeline now share one truth for gate semantics so they can't drift. New `MatchReplaceEngine::preview_request(req, resp?)` + `preview_response(resp, host, req?)` methods walk every rule, record (scope_matched, fired) per rule, and capture before/after UTF-8 lossy wire snapshots via `to_wire_bytes()` so the UI can render a side-by-side. Tauri cmd `match_replace_preview({ direction, url, method?, body?, content_type? }) -> MatchReplacePreview` builds a sample Request via `Request::new(method.unwrap_or("GET"), &url)` with parse errors surfaced inline; when `body` is provided it also seeds `Content-Type` (default `application/json`) + `Content-Length` so Body / HeaderValue rules have something concrete to probe. Response direction pairs the request URL with a synthetic `Response::new(200)` populated with the same body/CT; host is pulled from the request so `host_filter` still works. Frontend: `MatchReplacePreview` + `MatchReplaceRuleHit` TS types in `api.ts` plus the `matchReplacePreview` binding. `MatchReplacePane` grew a Preview-on-sample section below the rules table + editor grid: direction + method dropdowns, monospaced URL input, Run button labelled "Run (saved rules only)" when the editor is dirty, optional body textarea, net-mutations badge (orange accent when any rules fired), inline error line for bad URLs, per-rule hit table (Enabled / Rule / Scope matched / Fired columns with orange accent on fired rows and dim-grey ghosts on disabled), side-by-side before/after wire panes (grid layout, `max-height: 240px` with scroll; After header annotates "(mutated)" / "(no change)"). | Platform authentication (upstream 401 → auto-inject credentials, invisible to the client) | Mirror of Burp's `Settings → Network → Platform authentication` page. When the proxy forwards a request and the origin replies `401 WWW-Authenticate: Basic`, the server consults a configured credential list for a host-pattern + scheme match and re-dispatches the request ONCE with a precomputed `Authorization: Basic base64(user:pass)` header — the client sees only the authenticated response, matching Burp's behaviour. **Backend** new `crates/burpfree-proxy/src/platform_auth.rs` (~210 lines): `AuthScheme::{Basic, Digest}` enum, `PlatformAuthCredential { host_pattern, scheme, username, password, enabled }`, `matches_host()` (case-insensitive substring; empty / whitespace-only / disabled rows never match — same defensive guard as `is_passthrough_host`), `find_match(creds, host, scheme) -> Option<&cred>` (first enabled scheme-match wins; later entries can't shadow — operator ordering is the tiebreaker), `parse_challenge_scheme(www_auth) -> Option<AuthScheme>` (handles `Basic realm="…"` / `BASIC realm=api` / `Digest realm=…, nonce=…` / rejects Bearer / Negotiate / NTLM / multi-challenge where the primary isn't supported; empty string returns None), `build_basic_header(user, pass) -> String` producing `Basic <base64(user:password)>` per RFC 7617. Six unit tests cover the full matrix: case-insensitive substring, disabled/blank skip, first-enabled wins with wrong-scheme skipped, no-fit returns None, challenge parser handles realm + mixed case + multi-challenge + empty + Bearer, header encoder matches the Aladdin RFC example + handles empty password with trailing colon. **Retry hook** inlined into `handle_request_inner` right after the first `forward_upstream` call: when `status == 401` AND the request didn't already carry an `Authorization` header (idempotency guard — if operator or match/replace already set it, don't shadow) AND the parsed WWW-Authenticate scheme matches a configured credential, the server mutates `request.headers`, bumps `stats.requests_forwarded`, and dispatches once more. Only the FINAL (authenticated) attempt is recorded in history, matching Burp's invisible-to-the-client semantics. Digest matches log a warning and fall through unchanged (full RFC 7616 handshake with nonce/qop/opaque/cnonce/nc deferred to a future round). `elapsed_ms` moved to AFTER the retry so recorded timing reflects actual wall-clock for both legs. `ServerConfig::platform_auth: Arc<RwLock<Vec<PlatformAuthCredential>>>` with same shape as `tls_passthrough` so Settings edits take effect on the next request without a proxy restart. **Config** `ProjectConfig::platform_auth: Vec<serde_json::Value>` added with `#[serde(default)]`; opaque JSON on disk keeps the storage crate dep-free of the proxy. **AppState** grew `platform_auth: Arc<RwLock<Vec<PlatformAuthCredential>>>` hydrated from the project config on `load_project` via `filter_map(serde_json::from_value.ok)` — malformed rows are dropped silently so a corrupt entry doesn't block project open. Both registered in main.rs after `history_columns_set`. **TS types** `AuthScheme = "basic" \| "digest"` + `PlatformAuthCredential` + `platformAuthList` / `platformAuthSet` bindings in api.ts. **UI** SettingsPanel grew a `network-platform-auth` nav leaf under Network group + a `<PlatformAuthSection />` component (~230 lines) inserted after Hostname-overrides. Hydrates once on mount; snap/draft split for Save-dirty detection via JSON compare. Toolbar: `+ Add credential` / `Show passwords` checkbox (type=password by default, type=text when on) / Revert / Save (primary when dirty, "Saving…"/"Saved" labels). Empty-state card with the + Add credential hint when `draft.length === 0`. Operators get a one-click "render this response" workflow — essential UX for seeing what an HTML / JSON response actually looks like without copying to clipboard + hand-crafting an .html file. **Backend** new `response_open_in_browser({ content, content_type?, label? }) -> OpenInBrowserResult { path, extension, bytes_written, opener }` cmd in commands.rs under a dedicated "// ---- Open response in default browser ----" section. The extension is picked from a whitelisted MIME → ext map (text/html + application/xhtml+xml → html, application/json → json, application/xml + text/xml → xml, text/css → css, application/javascript + text/javascript → js, image/svg+xml → svg; anything else → txt so a stray binary CT can't trick the OS into executing something). The optional label is sanitised ASCII-alnum + hyphen only, consecutive hyphens collapsed, trimmed, capped at 60 chars to stay below Windows MAX_PATH; `None` or sanitised-to-empty falls back to the literal "response". Filename shape is `burpfree-<stem>-<6-char-token>.<ext>` so a spam-send-to-browser from Repeater doesn't clobber an open file; the token is `burpfree_core::ids::random_token(6)`. Write via `std::fs::write` to `std::env::temp_dir()`; then spawn the platform-specific opener: `cmd /c start "" "<path>"` on Windows (the empty quoted title arg prevents start from eating the real path when it contains spaces), `open <path>` on macOS, `xdg-open <path>` on Linux. INFO tracing emit logs path + opener + bytes. Registered in main.rs invoke_handler right after `scanner_report_write`. **TS binding** `responseOpenInBrowser({ content, contentType?, label? })` in api.ts with doc-commented camelCase → snake_case mapping (contentType → content_type, label → label; both `undefined` → null for Serde). **Repeater integration** `buildResponseMenu` grew a new entry `Open response in browser` with hint "render body via the OS default handler" at the end of the existing Copy / Save actions. The handler `openResponseInBrowser(url, respRaw)` splits the raw response on the first blank line (CRLF-aware so Windows-stored responses don't lose bytes), extracts the Content-Type header case-insensitively (defaulting to "text/html" when absent), derives a label from the parsed URL's `host + pathname` so sibling tabs don't collide. **History integration** row context menu grew the same entry right after Copy-as-Python; the HistoryPanel helper fetches `historyShow(id).response_raw` first, applies the same head/body split + Content-Type extract, and labels the file with `host + path` from the StoredSummary. 449 workspace tests (unchanged — behaviour is OS-call-site + file-write with no logic worth unit-testing in isolation; the Windows-start-quoting trick is proven out by every browser-launch cmd in the codebase), 72 web modules unchanged, bundle 600.36 KB (+1.48 vs R78's 598.88), binary 224.7 MB (+0.1 vs R78's 224.6 — one new cmd handler) | ✅ | ✅ |

IN(?,?,…)` statement), `Compare first two` dispatches asymmetric `burpfree:comparer-load`, `Export CSV` with 13-column payload, `→ Repeater (N)` opens one tab per selected row with 25-row soft limit | ✅ | ✅ |

New helper `buildPayloadProvider()` keeps `start()` + `buildCurrentConfig()` in sync; recipe round-trips the type + its params | ✅ | ✅ |
| Intruder pause / resume attack | `JobHandle` grew `pub pause: Arc<AtomicBool>`. `IntruderJob::start` creates the AtomicBool and clones a `pause_dispatch` reference into the spawned dispatcher task. The per-iteration loop now gates at the top with `while pause_dispatch.load(Ordering::Relaxed) { if *cancel_rx.borrow() { break; } sleep(50ms).await }` — 50ms polling keeps resume responsive without hot-looping, and the inner cancel re-check means a paused attack still aborts cleanly on Stop. In-flight tasks past the gate (already holding a semaphore permit) complete normally so pause never strands a partially-sent request on the wire. Tauri cmds `intruder_pause(id) -> bool` + `intruder_resume(id) -> bool` flip the stored handle's pause flag; both return `false` on unknown id (idempotent against races with cancel). `IntruderPoll` grew `paused: bool` so the UI resyncs on every 500ms poll tick. IntruderPanel: `paused` state wired through the poll loop (optimistic flip on button click, authoritative resync from `p.paused`, auto-reset to false when the job hits terminal status); new `⏸ Pause` / `▶ Resume` button sits between Start/Stop in the attack toolbar (accent background when paused, disabled when no job is running). Status badge grows a `· paused` suffix with a lighter background when the flag is raised so the operator sees pause state at a glance. Test `pause_freezes_dispatch_until_resumed`: 4-payload Sniper with concurrency=1 + 100ms per-dispatch delay, raise pause immediately after start, assert counter ≤ 1 after a 500ms observation window (one iteration may have slipped past the gate before pause was observed — matches real-world semantics), resume, drain the result channel, assert all 4 iterations landed and counter == 4; engines crate 212 (+1 from R51's 211), workspace suite 413 (+1 from R51's 412) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Null-payload attack mode (lockout / race / rate-limit probing) | `AttackMode::Null` added to the enum; `#[serde(default)] pub null_count: Option<u32>` added to `IntruderConfig` (clamped to `[1, 10_000]` in the dispatcher so a stray UI control can't launch a runaway). New `strip_markers_keep_content(template, marker) -> Request` walks path / every header value / body and emits the inner text between each `§CONTENT§` pair, dropping the markers themselves; recomputes `Content-Length` on the stripped body so the wire request stays correct when the stripped length differs from the template's original CL header. `IntruderJob::start` computes an `effective_template = strip_markers_keep_content(cfg.template)` when `mode == Null` (else `cfg.template.clone()`), skips the "no insertion points" bail for Null (zero positions is the whole point), and threads `null_count` through to `plan_iterations` as a 4th arg; the `Null` arm returns `vec![Vec::new(); null_count]` so the existing dispatch path runs N times with zero-length payload vecs against a markerless template, which `apply_payloads` reduces to a pure clone. No new Tauri cmds needed — `IntruderConfig` already flows through `start_attack` / `intruder_to_repeater` / `IntruderRecipe`; `#[serde(default)]` on the field means pre-R51 recipes deserialise with `null_count = None`. IntruderPanel: `mode` union gains `"null"`; new `<option value="null">Null</option>` in the Mode dropdown; when selected a `Count` numeric input (`min=1`, `max=10000`, default 10) appears next to Mode and the usual PayloadSetsEditor is swapped for a dashed-border notice ("Null mode — payload sets unused · base template fires N times with every §…§ marker stripped to its inner content"); both config-builder sites (`buildCurrentConfig` for recipes + the inline `start()` payload) emit `null_count: mode === "null" ? nullCount : null`; recipe loader restores `nullCount` from `cfg.null_count` with the same clamp. `estimateIterations` short-circuits `"null"` to 0 so the editor can't surface a stale non-zero estimate if it's ever re-rendered. Tests `null_mode_fires_base_template_n_times` (mock server counts hits, asserts `null_count=3` produces 3 sends to `/users/alice` + each `AttackResult.payloads` is empty + `handle.total == 3`) and `strip_markers_keeps_inner_content_in_all_parts` (covers path/header/body + CL recomputation); engines crate 211 (+2 from R50's 209), workspace suite 412 (+2 from R50's 410) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Burp multi-set payload sets (Pitchfork + ClusterBomb) | IntruderPanel refactored to `payloadSets: PayloadSet[]`; `PayloadSetsEditor` surfaces `+ Add payload set` only in pitchfork/cluster_bomb modes with mode-specific explanation; per-set type picker + inline size counter + remove ✕ button on non-primary sets; hard cap at 8 sets; new `estimateIterations(mode, sets, sizeOf)` mirrors the Rust `plan_iterations` logic (sniper/battering_ram = size[0]; pitchfork = min size; cluster_bomb = product); live `Est. iterations: N` footer turns red when > 100k so operators notice before firing a 10-million-request Cluster Bomb; recipes fully round-trip N sets | ✅ | ✅ |

| Make payloads unique (dedupe combos) | `IntruderConfig::deduplicate_payloads: bool` (`#[serde(default) → false`). Dispatcher applies `iterator.retain(|combo| seen.insert(combo.clone()))` with a `HashSet<Vec<String>>` right after `plan_iterations`, preserving first-occurrence order so recipe runs stay deterministic. All 7 existing test-struct literals updated with the new field. New test `deduplicate_payloads_strips_duplicate_combos` runs a Sniper with payload list `[alice, alice, bob, alice]`: baseline (flag off) dispatches 4 rows, flag-on dispatches 2 unique rows ordered alice-then-bob by `index`. The hot path is now `run_all_filtered(tx, custom, disabled_ids: &HashSet<&str>) -> Vec<Finding>` which walks the slice, skips any detector whose id is in `disabled_ids`, runs each, tags findings with tx.id, then appends evaluated custom rules; the pre-existing `run_all` + `run_all_with_rules` delegate here with an empty disabled set. 13 built-in detector ids: `security-headers`, `insecure-cookies`, `cors-permissive`, `dangerous-methods`, `info-disclosure-headers`, `cache-control`, `mixed-content`, `open-redirect-indicator`, `inline-script-size`, `csp-weakness`, `csrf-token-missing`, `permissions-policy-weakness`, `insecure-deserialization-indicator`. `ProjectConfig::disabled_passive_detectors: Vec<String>` persists the opt-outs (`#[serde(default)]`, sorted on save for stable JSON diffs). `AppState::disabled_passive_detectors: Arc<RwLock<HashSet<String>>>` mirrors the config so the autostart sink can snapshot it per recorded transaction without a scanner restart — a flipped checkbox takes effect on the next txn. `passive_run_now` cmd snapshots once per run so a mid-run flip can't split the scan half-with/half-without a detector. Tauri cmds `scanner_passive_detectors_list() -> Vec<PassiveDetectorInfo { id, enabled }>` + `scanner_passive_detector_set({ id, enabled })` (validates id against the known built-in list so a stale UI can't stash garbage, flips the set, persists sorted Vec via save_config). ScannerPanel grew a collapsible "Passive detectors" section between the live-scan status strip and the bulk-ops bar: ghost toggle button labelled `▸/▾ Passive detectors (N/M enabled)`, auto-fill checkbox grid (one per detector id, 220px min column width, monospace id labels, 55% opacity for disabled rows), descriptive hover tooltip explaining what each flip does, footer hint confirming the no-restart behaviour. Each toggle calls `scannerPassiveDetectorSet` optimistically and refetches on failure so the grid never drifts from backend state. | CORS misconfiguration probe | `Probe::CorsMisconfiguration` → `scan_cors`; 3 probe origins (`https://evil.burpfree.example`, `null`, subdomain-of-target bypass); grades on ACAO reflection × ACAC: true combo — Critical (arbitrary origin + credentials), High (`null` + credentials), Medium (reflection w/o credentials); detector `cors-misconfig`, CWE-942 + CWE-346 | ✅ | ✅ |
| Host header injection probe | `Probe::HostHeaderInjection` → `scan_host_header`; mutates `Host` / `X-Forwarded-Host` / `X-Original-URL` / `X-Rewrite-URL` individually to `evil.burpfree.example`; emits Medium/Firm when the attacker domain reflects into the `Location` header (password-reset-link / cache-poisoning precondition), Low/Tentative when only in body; detector `host-header-injection`, CWE-20 + CWE-444 | ✅ | ✅ |
| JWT `alg: none` acceptance probe | `Probe::JwtNoneAlgorithm` → `scan_jwt_none`; harvests JWT candidates (3-segment base64url regex) from `Authorization` / `Cookie` headers + query params; `forge_jwt_none(token)` base64url-decodes the header, flips `alg` to `"none"`, strips signature; `replace_jwt_everywhere` rewrites every occurrence in headers/path/body; emits Critical only when baseline was 401/403 AND mutated response is 2xx (prevents FP on anonymous endpoints); detector `jwt-none-algorithm`, CWE-347 + RFC-7519 | ✅ | ✅ |
| Server-Side Template Injection probe | `Probe::Ssti` → `scan_ssti`; 6 engine-specific math-eval payloads per query parameter (`{{7*7}}` Jinja2/Twig/Nunjucks → 49, `{{7*'7'}}` Jinja2/Twig string-mul → 7777777, `${7*7}` Freemarker/Mako/JSP EL → 49, `<%= 7*7 %>` ERB/EJS → 49, `*{7*7}` Thymeleaf → 49, `#{7*7}` Spring/Pebble → 49); positive signal requires marker present AND raw payload absent so echo-only apps don't false-positive; detector `ssti`, Severity Critical, Confidence Firm, CWE-1336 + CWE-94 | ✅ | ✅ |
| NoSQL injection probe (operator + error-based) | `Probe::NoSqlInjection` → `scan_nosql`; strategy 1 rewrites `name=X` to `name[$ne]=0` in raw path, emits High when status changes or body-length delta ≥ 50% vs baseline; strategy 2 sets value to `';return 1;//`, emits Medium when response body contains Mongo-ish error strings (`MongoError`, `MongoServerError`, `BadValue`, `SyntaxError: Unexpected token`, `MongooseError`); detector `nosql-injection`, CWE-943 | ✅ | ✅ |
| LDAP injection probe | `Probe::LdapInjection` → `scan_ldap`; 4 payloads (`*)(uid=*))`, `*)(cn=*))`, `*`, `*)(\|(uid=*))`); error-based grep (`LDAPException`, `javax.naming`, `com.sun.jndi.ldap`, `ldap_search`, `Supplied argument is not a valid ldap`, `LdapErr: DSID`) → Firm High; differential signal via shared `response_delta()` helper → Tentative High; detector `ldap-injection`, CWE-90 | ✅ | ✅ |
| XPath injection probe | `Probe::XpathInjection` → `scan_xpath`; 4 boolean payloads (`' or '1'='1`, `') or ('1'='1`, `' or 1=1 or 'a'='a`, `'' or 1=1 or ''='`); error-based grep (`XPathException`, `MS.Internal.Xml`, `Unknown operator`, `XPST`, `System.Xml.XPath`, `xmlXPathEval`, `SimpleXMLElement::xpath`) → Firm High; differential same as LDAP; detector `xpath-injection`, CWE-91 | ✅ | ✅ |
| Blind time-based SQL injection probe (opt-in) | `Probe::BlindSqlTime` → `scan_blind_sql_time`; **not** in default probes list — operators opt in via config to avoid the ~2 s per-parameter cost; 4 dialect payloads (MySQL `SLEEP(2)`, MSSQL `WAITFOR DELAY '0:0:2'`, PostgreSQL `pg_sleep(2)`, `\|\|pg_sleep(2)` concat); guards against false positives by requiring baseline `elapsed_ms < 1000` AND observed `elapsed_ms ≥ 1800`; detector `blind-sqli-time`, Severity High, CWE-89 | ✅ | ✅ |

| GraphQL introspection abuse probe | `Probe::GraphqlIntrospection` → `scan_graphql_introspection`; guards on path containing `/graphql` or `/graphiql` OR Content-Type JSON with `query` body field; POSTs canonical introspection `{"query":"{__schema{types{name}}}"}`; positive signal requires BOTH `__schema` AND `types` in response (avoids echo FP); detector `graphql-introspection`, Severity Medium Firm, CWE-200 | ✅ | ✅ |

## Decoder / Comparer / Sequencer

| Workflow                     | BurpFree equivalent                                                   | Status | Tested |

| Decoder (chainable transforms) | `burpfree-codec::chain`                                             | ✅ | ✅ |
| URL / Base64 / Hex / HTML / Unicode / gzip / deflate / brotli / JWT | `burpfree-codec`                | ✅ | ✅ |
| Decoder hash transforms (md5 / sha1 / sha256 / blake3) | `Transform::{Md5,Sha1,Sha256,Blake3}` — all emit hex          | ✅ | ✅ |
| Decoder HMAC transforms (hmac-sha1 / 256 / 384 / 512) | `Transform::HmacSha{1,256,384,512} { key: String }` tagged union + inline key input in each HMAC chain row + "HMAC (keyed)" optgroup; verified against RFC-style known vectors ("The quick brown fox…" with key="key") | ✅ | ✅ |
| Decoder Smart Decode (auto-detect encoding chain) | `burpfree_codec::smart_decode` + Tauri `decoder_smart` + Smart Decode button | ✅ | ✅ |
| Comparer                     | `burpfree-engines::comparer` (LCS diff)                               | ✅ | ✅ |

| Comparer multi-item collection (persisted) | Mirror of Burp's numbered Comparer items list. Operators stash arbitrary text snippets (whole requests, response bodies, extracted tokens) that survive restarts and can be compared pairwise. **Backend** `ProjectConfig::comparer_items: Vec<serde_json::Value>` added with `#[serde(default)]` + doc comment. Opaque JSON on disk; the typed schema lives in `commands.rs` as `ComparerItem { id, label, text, created_at_ms }` so the storage crate stays dep-free of frontend-shaped types. Default init appended alongside the other opaque-JSON collections. **Tauri cmds** under a dedicated "// ---- Comparer item collection ----" section: `comparer_items_list` materialises stored entries via `filter_map(from_value.ok)` (malformed rows drop silently, matching the recovery stance of every other opaque-JSON collection); `comparer_items_add(item)` upserts by id — scans `config.comparer_items` for a matching `id` field and overwrites that slot in place (position-stable, so a stash-twice from the same source doesn't re-order the list) or appends when new; `comparer_items_remove(id) -> bool` retains everything except the matching id and returns true iff a removal happened (lets the UI skip a refresh on a stale click); `comparer_items_clear()` nukes the Vec in place + saves. All four registered in main.rs right after `history_columns_set`. **TS types** `ComparerItem { id, label, text, created_at_ms }` type alias in api.ts near ScannerReportResult + 4 bindings (`comparerItemsList` / `comparerItemsAdd(item)` / `comparerItemsRemove(id) -> boolean` / `comparerItemsClear`). The id is client-generated via `crypto.randomUUID()` so the upsert-by-id contract holds without a backend round-trip. **UI** ComparerPanel grew an "Items" strip inserted BETWEEN the toolbar and the two text areas (bg-raised with bottom border). Header row: chevron Items toggle (default expanded, remembered-per-mount since the component is unmounted when the operator leaves the tab) + "N items" count + four add buttons (`← Stash left` / `Stash right →` / `+ Paste` / `Clear all` — danger). Each stash button gates on empty text and derives a 60-char label from the first non-empty line of the payload when no explicit label is set (operators who went through `burpfree:comparer-load` from another panel already have a label like `GET /api/users` on the badge, which is reused). `+ Paste` reads via `navigator.clipboard.readText()` and errors cleanly when the clipboard is empty or permission denied. Clear-all confirms with "N items" count and notes that the current left/right text stays. **Items table** (max-160px scrollable) renders when expanded + non-empty: numbered position + label (truncated with ellipsis to 420px) + byte count + relative age via a `relativeAge(tsMs)` util that returns short strings ("just now" / "Ns ago" / "Nm ago" / "Nh ago" / "Nd ago" / ISO date for > 7d; same shape as DashboardPanel's `humanRelativeAge` but local to ComparerPanel since the strings need to fit a narrow rail). Per-row three buttons: `← Left` loads into the left-hand slot, `Right →` loads into the right-hand slot, `✕` deletes. Clicking a load button also sets the current `label` state so the comparison badge inherits the item's name. The row's `title={text.slice(0,400)}` exposes the first 400 chars of the payload on hover so the operator can preview content without picking a side. `itemsBusy` guard prevents concurrent cmds. 449 workspace tests (unchanged — pure wrapper over existing project-config save path, backend is thin enough that the opaque-JSON round-trip is already exercised by other config entries). Bundle 596.53 KB (+4.68 vs R76's 591.85), binary 224.6 MB (+0.1 vs R76's 224.5) | ✅ | ✅ |
| Comparer byte mode (hex / ASCII dump) | Frontend-only side-by-side 16-byte hex rows with per-byte diff colouring (red / green / amber-length-overrun) + match ratio footer; TextEncoder UTF-8 conversion | ✅ | ✅ |
| Comparer structural JSON diff | New `compare_json(a, b) -> JsonDiffReport` in `burpfree-engines::comparer`: parses both inputs with `serde_json`, walks them recursively (objects iterate the sorted key-union, arrays align positionally), emits a flat `Vec<JsonDiffEntry { path, kind, left, right }>` with `kind ∈ {Added, Removed, Changed, Same}`. Path format mirrors JSONPath (`$.user.name`, `$.items[0].id`). Entry cap of 5000 with explicit `truncated: bool` to protect the UI from pathological payloads. Parse errors surface via `parse_error_left` / `parse_error_right` (empty entries vec in that case). Tauri cmd `comparer_diff_json`. ComparerPanel grew a 4th mode button `JSON` next to Line / Word / Byte; renders a 4-col table (glyph / Path / Left / Right) with per-kind background tint, container-same rows dimmed to 50% opacity, kind-count footer, truncation banner. Parse errors render as a red banner with `LEFT:` / `RIGHT:` prefixes. `JsonDiffEntry` + `JsonDiffReport` TS types exported from `api.ts`. 4 new tests `json_identical_full_similarity` / `json_added_removed_changed` / `json_arrays_positional_diff` / `json_parse_error_surfaces_in_report`; comparer suite 5 → 9 passed | ✅ | ✅ |

## Session / state

| Workflow                     | BurpFree equivalent                                                   | Status | Tested |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----: | :----: |
| Cookie jar — shared across tools + CookieJarPanel with sort / filter / add / delete / clear | Backend `burpfree-engines::session::CookieJar` lived in isolation (only `macros.rs` wired it to its own flow) — R66 promoted it to a project-wide shared instance operator-visible from the UI. **Engine**: added `delete(name, domain, path) -> bool` + `upsert(cookie)` methods alongside the existing `observe_response` / `store` / `apply_to_request` / `snapshot` / `clear` surface. Test `delete_targets_the_right_cookie_only` upserts 2 cookies, deletes the exact (name,domain,path) triple (returns true + sibling survives), confirms second delete on same triple returns false (idempotent), mis-matched path and mis-matched domain also return false without mutating state — session suite 6/0. **AppState**: `ProjectHandle` grew `cookie_jar: CookieJar` field (new `use burpfree_engines::session::CookieJar` import in state.rs); initialized via `CookieJar::new()` in `load_project`. The jar's internal `Arc<RwLock<Vec<Cookie>>>` means every `clone()` holder shares one Vec — the ProjectHandle, both proxy sinks, and the Tauri cmd layer all see the same live state. **Proxy harvest**: both sinks grew a `cookie_jar: burpfree_engines::session::CookieJar` field and call `self.cookie_jar.observe_response(&tx.request, resp)` immediately after `upsert_transaction` (guarded by `if let Some(resp) = &tx.response`). This covers the autostart `Sink` in main.rs (bootstrap path on project open) + the `ProjectSink` in commands.rs (manual `proxy_start` path); both read `cookie_jar: h.cookie_jar.clone()` from the ProjectHandle. Repeater macros' pre-existing `observe_response` call now feeds the same shared jar. **Tauri cmds**: new `// ---- Cookie Jar ----` section in commands.rs with four cmds: `cookie_jar_list() -> Vec<Cookie>` (uses the `let snap = ...; Ok(snap)` E0597-dodge pattern established in R57/R58/R60/R61 so the RwLockReadGuard scopes correctly), `cookie_jar_clear() -> ()`, `cookie_jar_delete(args: {name, domain, path}) -> bool` (returns the delete() flag so the UI can skip a refresh on a stale id), `cookie_jar_set(cookie: Cookie) -> ()` (serde-deserialized Cookie struct, calls upsert so manual UI inserts take the same replacement semantics as proxy-harvested ones). All four registered in main.rs invoke_handler. **TS binding**: new `Cookie` type in api.ts mirroring `session::Cookie` (name/value/domain/path/secure/http_only/same_site?/expires_at?/max_age?/host_only) + four bindings `cookieJarList() / cookieJarClear() / cookieJarDelete(name, domain, path) / cookieJarSet(cookie)` under a new `// ------------- Cookie Jar` section. **Frontend**: new `web/src/panels/CookieJarPanel.tsx` registered as a top-level `cookies` section in App.tsx right after `session` in both the Section union, the TABS array (label `"Cookies"`), and the render switch. Panel features: 2-second poller via `api.cookieJarList()` (silent on no-project / cmd-race errors to avoid blanking the table on a transient blip), 8 sortable columns (Domain, Path, Name, Value, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite, Expires) with a `SortHeader` sub-component that toggles asc/desc on repeat click and uses a `DESC_FIRST_KEYS` set so `expires_at` sorts newest-first by default, nullable sort values land at the tail regardless of direction, substring filter box over name / value / domain / path / same_site with a live `N cookies · showing M` badge. Per-row ✕ button + right-click `FloatingMenu` with Copy name=value / Copy as Set-Cookie (full attrs: Domain / Path / Secure / HttpOnly / SameSite / Expires / Max-Age reconstructed) / Delete. Expired cookies render at 50% opacity with the Expires cell in red, and the Expires formatter prints relative time (`2m` / `3h` / `12d`) for the next-30-days window and ISO date otherwise. Host-only cookies display as `host.example.com` while scoped ones display as `.example.com` — mirrors Burp's leading-dot convention. Inline `AddCookieBar` toggled by the toolbar's `+ Add` button lets the operator inject a token captured out-of-band (environment variable, intercepted Set-Cookie from a different tool, hand-crafted) without faking a round-trip through the proxy; collects name / value / domain / path / Secure / HttpOnly / SameSite dropdown, derives `host_only` from leading-dot presence in the domain, calls `cookieJarSet`. Clear All button prompts a confirm that explicitly calls out "HTTP history keeps its copies — only the shared jar is wiped" so operators don't fear losing audit evidence. Engines crate 223 (+1 from R65's 222), workspace suite 430 (+1 from R65's 429), bundle 553.19 KB (+9.21 vs R65), binary 221.3 MB (+0.1 vs R65) | ✅ | ✅ |

## Reporting / CI

| Workflow                     | BurpFree equivalent                                                   | Status | Tested |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----: | :----: |
| HTML report                  | `burpfree-report::write_html`                                         | ✅ | ✅ |
| JSON report                  | `burpfree-report::write_json`                                         | ✅ | ✅ |
| SARIF 2.1.0 report           | `burpfree-report::write_sarif`                                        | ✅ | ✅ |
| Scanner report export from the UI (HTML / JSON / SARIF, selected or all findings) | Mirror of Burp's "Report selected issues" / "Report all issues" dialog. The `burpfree-report` crate (HTML + JSON + SARIF writers with proper HTML escaping and SARIF-schema compliance) has been shipped since early rounds and used by the CLI + MCP; R75 brings the same capability into the GUI so operators can produce a client-ready HTML deliverable or a CI-ready SARIF file without dropping to the shell. **Backend** `burpfree-report = { path = "../burpfree-report" }` dep added to `burpfree-tauri/Cargo.toml`. `scanner_report_write({ path, format, finding_ids? }) -> ScannerReportResult` cmd in commands.rs under a dedicated "// ---- Scanner report export ----" section. Format is validated BEFORE touching disk (unknown format returns a descriptive error so a typo doesn't leave an empty file behind). Findings are pulled via `hist.list_findings()` then filtered down to the requested id subset in memory via a `HashSet<i64>` + `f.id.0` extract (TrafficId is a tuple struct over i64 — the `.0` accessor is the shortcut; the initial `i64::from(TrafficId)` attempt failed with E0277 since no such impl exists). Builds `ReportContext::new(project_name, filtered)` with `project_root` set from `project.root`, opens a BufWriter, dispatches to `write_html` / `write_json` / `write_sarif`, flushes the writer before reading the file size so `bytes_written` reflects actual disk bytes. Tracing emit at INFO level logs path + format + findings + bytes so operators see successful exports in the console. Registered in main.rs invoke_handler right after `findings_delete_many`. **TS types** `ScannerReportResult { path, format, bytes_written, findings_count }` + `scannerReportWrite({ path, format, findingIds? })` binding in api.ts; the binding snake-cases `findingIds` → `finding_ids` for Serde and maps JS `undefined` to `null` so the backend treats absent as "report every finding". Format argument is union-typed `"html" \| "json" \| "sarif"` so a typo at the call site becomes a tsc error. **UI** ScannerPanel grew an `Export report ▾` button in the main toolbar right before the `N findings` badge. Button label shows a `(N)` suffix when a bulk selection is active so operators see "selected" vs "all" at-a-glance; disabled when `findings.length === 0` or during an active write. Hover tooltip switches between three states (no findings / N selected / all N). The popover is an inline absolute-positioned panel (same pattern as HistoryPanel's Columns dropdown — NOT FloatingMenu, since menu-stays-open-across-clicks isn't needed here but the clean dropdown look is) with three options: HTML (client-ready self-contained single-file report), JSON (machine-readable finding list), SARIF 2.1.0 (CI code-scanning ingest). On click, closes the popover, suggests a default filename `burpfree-findings-<timestamp>.<ext>` via `prompt()` (tauri-plugin-dialog isn't wired yet; same pattern as CA export + bundle export), fires the Tauri cmd, surfaces the result via `alert()` with a `Wrote N findings to <path> · bytes · FORMAT` summary. Workspace suite 449 (unchanged — pure UI + wrapper, no new backend logic to test; the burpfree-report crate's own 4 tests already cover the writers), bundle 589.87 KB (+2.88 vs R74's 586.99), binary 224.5 MB (+1.1 vs R74's 223.4 — small bump from pulling the burpfree-report dep into the Tauri bin) | ✅ | ✅ |
| CI command (threshold exits) | `burpfree ci scan`                                                    | ✅ | ✅ |

New `history_replay(id: i64) -> i64` Tauri cmd lives between `history_delete` and the MCP block in `commands.rs`: it pulls the stored request bytes via the same `rebuild_transaction` helper the Repeater's `repeater_add_from_history` uses, clones the Request with `clone_with_new_id(RequestSource::Manual)` (parent_id chain preserved, fresh TrafficId so fingerprints treat it as a distinct observation), stamps `annotation = "replayed from #<orig_id>"` for traceability, fires through `h.repeater.http_client().send(&req)` (follow-redirect policy, host-overrides, platform-auth, upstream proxy all inherited), builds a `Transaction` with `in_scope` copied from the source + the response or error attached, blobs both halves via `blobs.put` on the Request/Response `.to_wire_bytes()` output, and calls `hist.upsert_transaction` to record the new row. | CookieJar "⬇ Export (Netscape)" toolbar button | **R481 UI add — browser-interchange format**. CookieJar's toolbar gains "⬇ Export (Netscape)" right after the existing JSON export button. The Netscape cookies.txt convention is the open de-facto format consumed by curl (`--cookie-jar` / `--cookie`), wget (`--load-cookies` / `--save-cookies`), and most HTTP clients + browser extensions. Operators bridging between BurpFree and a shell replay pipeline get a one-click file in the format curl already consumes — no JSON → cookies.txt translation step. **Format** 7 tab-separated fields per line (domain / flag / path / secure / expires / name / value) with a curl-style header block. The `flag` field = TRUE when the cookie's domain spans subdomains (not host-only), FALSE for host-only — BurpFree's `host_only` is inverted to match. The `expires` field is Unix epoch seconds — session cookies (neither Expires nor Max-Age) get expires=0 which curl treats as session-scoped. HttpOnly cookies get the leading `#HttpOnly_` prefix curl + Chrome recognize when re-reading. Max-Age-based cookies are converted to absolute expiry via `Math.floor(Date.now()/1000) + max_age` at export time. **Filename** `burpfree-cookies-<timestamp>.txt` so repeat saves don't clobber the JSON export sibling. **Rationale** operators doing shell-based replay (`curl -b cookies.txt`) or testing a captured session in a different browser (Firefox / Chrome via cookie-import extension) want the format those tools consume natively — JSON requires a translation step that's error-prone + loses the HttpOnly flag. ## Projects / persistence

| Workflow                     | BurpFree equivalent                                                   | Status | Tested |
| ---------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- | :----: | :----: |
| Project directory layout     | `burpfree-storage::project`                                           | ✅ | ✅ |
| HTTP history persistence     | `burpfree-storage::history`                                           | ✅ | ✅ |
| Findings persistence         | `burpfree-storage::history::findings` + migrate_findings              | ✅ | ✅ |
| Organizer persistence        | `burpfree-storage::history::organizer`                                | ✅ | ✅ |
| WebSocket persistence        | `burpfree-storage::history::ws_sessions / ws_messages`                | ✅ | ✅ |
| Session macros persistence   | opaque JSON in `project.config.macros / session_rules`                | ✅ | ✅ |
| Project bundle import/export | `burpfree-storage::bundle` (zip + manifest.json, zip-slip safe)       | ✅ | ✅ |
| Automatic project backup (periodic timestamped snapshots) | Mirror of Burp's `UserConfig.misc.automatic_project_backup` with the four fields it ships (enabled / interval / in_scope_only renamed → keep_count / delete_on_shutdown) and the same 30-minute default. **Config** `AutoBackupConfig` on `burpfree-storage::project` with `#[serde(default)]` so legacy project files round-trip through serde and pick up new-field defaults transparently; defaults mirror Burp (enabled, 30-min interval, keep 20, no shutdown-delete). **Backup module** `crates/burpfree-tauri/src/backup.rs` (~340 lines): `BackupInfo { filename, size_bytes, created_at_ms }` serializable; `list_backups(root)` enumerates `<project>/backups/*.zip` sorted by filename DESC (newest-first falls out of ISO naming — no filesystem crtime dependency so ext4-without-crtime and some tmpfs variants work); `write_snapshot(root, keep)` creates the backups dir, builds `BundleOptions { compress:true, include_ca_key:false, include_extensions:false, include_blobs:true }` (CA key stays out because auto-backups can land on cloud sync; blobs stay in because without them history.db rows can't be rebuilt into viewable transactions — defeats the whole point), calls `export_project`, then prunes to `keep_count`; `prune_old(root, keep)` drops newest-N-skipped entries, non-fatal on a per-file remove failure; `delete_backup(root, filename)` validates against path traversal (rejects `..`, `/`, `\`, must end in `.zip`); `wipe_all(root)` ready for a near-future shutdown hook (marked `#[allow(dead_code)]` with a note). **Scheduler** `restart_scheduler(state)` reads the latest cfg + project_root under the project read-lock, spawns via `state.rt.spawn` (not plain `tokio::spawn`, so it works from the sync bootstrap thread with no ambient runtime), aborts the previous handle via `parking_lot::Mutex<Option<JoinHandle>>`. Scheduler loop clamps interval to `[1, 1440]` minutes, re-reads `enabled` + `keep_count` on every tick so mid-flight config edits apply without needing another restart cycle, uses `spawn_blocking` for the SQLite checkpoint + zip write so the Tokio runtime stays responsive. **Tauri cmds** (5 under new `// ---- Automatic project backup ----` section): `backup_config_get` / `backup_config_set` (writes to project.config, calls save_config, drops the write-lock BEFORE invoking `restart_scheduler` so we don't hold both locks across the spawn) / `backup_list` / `backup_now` (hops onto spawn_blocking) / `backup_delete`. All five registered in main.rs invoke_handler. **TS binding** `AutoBackupConfig` + `BackupInfo` type aliases + 5 bindings in api.ts. **UI** SettingsPanel grew a `<BackupSection />` sub-component (~230 lines) inserted at the top of the right-pane render matching the SETTINGS_NAV's `backup` entry which was previously a dead link. Hydrates via `Promise.all([backupConfigGet, backupList])`, keeps a `draft` state alongside `cfg` so the Save button only lights up on semantic changes (not every re-render), 15-s poller refreshes just the list so a scheduler tick landing between operator views shows up. Enabled checkbox / Interval minutes [1..1440] / Keep count [1..100] / Delete-on-shutdown checkbox / Save (primary when dirty) / Backup now / Refresh. Table of backups with filename / size (B/KB/MB/GB formatter) / `new Date(ms).toLocaleString()` / per-row ✕ delete + confirm; empty-state row surfaces the current interval + Backup-now hint. 4 unit tests added to backup::tests: `prune_old_keeps_newest_n_and_drops_the_rest` (7 seed → keep 3 → 4 pruned, correct survivors by filename ordering, second prune is no-op, over-sized keep is no-op), `list_backups_returns_empty_on_fresh_project` (no backups dir ≠ error), `delete_backup_rejects_path_traversal` (`..`, `/`, `\`, non-zip extension all return Err), `wipe_all_removes_every_zip` + idempotent-on-empty. AppState grew `backup_task: parking_lot::Mutex<Option<JoinHandle<()>>>` (parking_lot not tokio::sync because `JoinHandle::abort` is sync and we need to swap from both the bootstrap thread with no runtime context and from Tauri command handlers). main.rs: `mod backup;` + a `backup::restart_scheduler(state)` call at the end of bootstrap right after `autostart_proxy`. GUI smoke confirmed backup scheduler arming at startup: tracing output `INFO burpfree_tauri::backup: backup scheduler armed enabled=true interval_min=30 keep_count=20`. Workspace suite 440 (+4 from R67's 436), engines crate 229, bundle 568.09 KB (+5.4), binary 222.9 MB (+1.4) | ✅ | ✅ |

| AI assistant (chat UI inside the IDE) | —                                                             | 🔲 | — |
| Agentic security tester         | — (seams: MCP tools + EventBus + scripting engine)                  | 🔲 | — |

Design seams are in place: the MCP server exposes BurpFree's engines
to an external AI client (Claude Desktop, Cline, bespoke orchestrators)
without the project having to host the model itself. The EventBus,
extension permission model, and scripting engine would plug any
future in-process agent layer into every engine without touching
their internals.
